title: Feeling lets an organism choose when it cannot predict the outcome

statements.text: In predictable situations an organism can rely on reflexes and on predictions built in by natural selection. To choose well in novel contexts it must assess the relative value of the alternatives here and now, and it does so by feeling its way through the problem, the direction of feeling predicting the direction of expected uncertainty. This is why consciousness arises and why, once evolved, it was conserved.

sources.quote: feeling enables complex organisms to register—and thereby to regulate and prioritize through thinking and voluntary action—deviations from homeostatic settling points in unpredicted contexts
it does so by feeling its way through the problem
This, in our view, is why consciousness arises.
